messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — hitting a weird edge when cancelling async streams in py-sdk. After the generator exits the underlying TCP socket sometimes stays ESTABLISHED (seen with lsof).

Maya Patel: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro?

Alex Chen: Quick repro below (very small). Observed behavior: break out of the async for, expect socket closed, but it remains open.

```py
# repro (simplified)
async with client.stream("/v1/stream", ... ) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream:
        if chunk == "stop":
            break
# expected: transport closed when stream context exits
await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
# lsof shows python -> TCP socket still ESTABLISHED
```

Sam Ortiz: We saw something similar before — ordering of finalizers/weakref vs transport close can leak the socket. If aclose isn't awaited because the generator was cancelled/broken it's possible the lower-level transport never got closed.

Priya Singh: I tried calling `await stream.aclose()` in a finally block and on some runs it fixes it, on others (uvloop vs asyncio) the socket still lingers until GC. Looks nondeterministic.

Ryan Gomez: Which py-sdk version + python + uvloop? Also please enable debug logs: `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and paste output.

Alex Chen: py-sdk 0.8.3, CPython 3.10.8, uvloop 0.15.2. Logs attached to GH repro I made (see link below). Also seeing a stray empty final chunk in a few runs right before the socket stays open.

Maya Patel: Hm — could be the SSE/chunked parser not draining the httpx transport when the generator is closed early. If the parser yields then leaves unread bytes in the connection, connection pooling might keep it alive.

Sam Ortiz: Agreed. Quick mitigation: ensure our stream wrapper always calls `await stream._resp.aclose()` (or httpx.Response.aclose()) in the finally path of the async generator wrapper. Also make sure to drain/read until EOF before returning to the pool.

Priya Singh: I filed GH issue #1425 with a tiny repro, lsof output, and a CI job that runs it under uvloop. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/issues/1425

Ryan Gomez: Thanks. Adding to eng-runtime backlog and assigning to someone to investigate kernel-level fd hold. Can you add a test that asserts the fd is closed (psutil or lsof) so we catch regressions? Also include REDWOOD_DEBUG logs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: prod deploy for 2026-03-20 finished :rocket:

Alex Chen: For teams blocked in the meantime — workaround is to wrap consumption and call `await stream.aclose()` in a finally or explicitly call `await response.aclose()` on the underlying response object. I'll add a short note to the streaming docs.

Maya Patel: Filing a small docs PR would help. Also Sam — can you prototype the change to our wrapper to always drain or aclose in the generator finalizer?

Sam Ortiz: Yep, I'll put up a draft fix + unit tests that assert socket closed across uvloop and stdlib loop.
